subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `captionedFinalText` as a public channel Plugin SDK capability for generic core dispatch, or keep this Telegram behavior behind a narrower internal seam?
rationale: The patch is a plausible plugin-agnostic repair, but it creates a durable extension-facing contract whose incorrect use can alter or suppress message delivery; tests cannot decide whether maintainers want to own that API.

options.title: Accept the typed capability after proof
options.body: Approve the opt-in SDK contract and require current-head Telegram proof plus green required checks before merge.

options.title: Use a narrower Telegram seam
options.body: Keep the user-facing fix but avoid a public capability until another caption-capable channel establishes the generic contract.

options.title: Pause the delivery-policy change
options.body: Do not merge until maintainers choose a stable long-term boundary for captioned final TTS delivery.

recommendation.title: Accept the typed capability after proof
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in SDK contract and require current-head Telegram proof plus green required checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history ties this person most directly to the affected TTS capability and outbound delivery surfaces.
